d: An upgrowth of oral (surface) ectoderm from the roof of the embryonic mouth that becomes the anterior pituitary; its remnants can later give rise to a craniopharyngioma.

Capillaries in the median eminence that collect hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones and drain through portal veins into a second capillary bed in the anterior pituitary, delivering them in high concentration.
Swellings of hypothalamic axon endings in the posterior pituitary that store ADH or oxytocin bound to its carrier protein, neurophysin, until an action potential releases it into the blood.
The large precursor protein in corticotrophs that is cut into ACTH, beta-endorphin and melanocyte-stimulating hormone, so conditions with high ACTH also darken the skin.
The venous space beside the sella that holds the internal carotid artery and cranial nerves III, IV, V1, V2 and VI, so a pituitary mass that grows sideways causes double vision and facial numbness.
